mvpRouteSearchPolicy: The L3 solver stops at the first verified winning candidate. Promotion preserves a retained route that still wins, regardless of survivor or input count.

sourceRuleReferences.claim: The manual says Mole creatures start digging when they hit bricks or steel, then bounce off those materials while tunnelling.
A player who owned the game reports that the Mole starts digging on bricks or steel and bounces off them while tunnelling.
The Shadow Tribe level 7 walkthrough uses a vertical stack of four or five bricks to direct the Mole into a tunnel that frees the embedded Spades.

mvpPromotionCheck.result: KEPT MVP 001: retained route wins. The CLI validated the retained fixture twice and skipped the search.

mvpRouteRepairProbes.source: Shadow Tribe level 7 walkthrough: use bricks to direct the Mole and release the embedded Spades.
observations: The upRight build triggered a downRight Mole tunnel, but none of the four Spade pickups were released; the route ended at tick 2600 with 0 saved.
The vertical build at tick 615 triggered a downLeft tunnel. The Mole passed below the embedded Spades; the route ended at tick 2600 with 0 saved.
The vertical build at tick 690 triggered a downRight tunnel. The Mole reached x266,y181, below the embedded Spades, and did not release them; the route ended at tick 2600 with 0 saved.
mvpRouteRepairProbes.result: No route won and no fixture changed. This narrows the source-guided route gap to Mole direction, tunnel placement or excavation around the embedded pickups; it does not prove which runtime rule differs from the original game.

mvpRouteRepairProbes.result: No candidate route won twice. No fixture changed.

mvpRouteRepairProbes.source: Shadow Tribe level 7 walkthrough: place a vertical brick stack by the pit wall, then jump off after the Mole starts tunnelling.
observations: The builder placed the stack at x188. The Mole started a down-left tunnel by tick 700, then later reached x240,y136.
The embedded Spade boxes remained available. Two boxes fell by 2 to 6 pixels, but no lemming collected them.
The route trace ended at tick 2200 with 0 saved. The input fixture was not changed.
mvpRouteRepairProbes.result: This source-guided stack-and-jump attempt did not produce an MVP win. It confirms a pickup-access or tunnel-clearance issue in this route, but it does not isolate the original-engine rule.

mvpPolicyDiscovery.policies: Existing deterministic discovery policies -1 through 7, evaluated on the current runtime library.
mvpPolicyDiscovery.provenanceLimit: The retained executable predates the current main.swift changes. The discovery policy bodies are unchanged; the source edits change retained-route handling and stop after the first route. Treat these results as bounded diagnostics, not strict-gate evidence.

originalEngineCaptureAttempt.method: Headless session with the local DOSBox web API. Read CPU and memory state and sent one Enter through the BIOS keyboard buffer.
originalEngineCaptureAttempt.observed: The game changed VGA graphics modes, but the memory dump did not yield a readable level image or controlled actor trace.
originalEngineCaptureAttempt.limitation: The exposed API provided CPU and memory endpoints, but no screenshot or timed input endpoint.
originalEngineCaptureAttempt.result: No original-engine rule was confirmed, no route or fixture changed, and no Mole or route gap closed.

egyptian6MvpRouteDiagnosis.routeGoal: One verified winning route at population 20. Do not optimise rescue count or input count.
egyptian6MvpRouteDiagnosis.walkthroughSummary: The Egyptian 6 walkthrough uses a vertical brick stack to reach a Shimmy pickup, then places a brick to trigger the Mole and opens a route down to the lower exits.

retainedFixtureTrace.inputs: The retained fixture starts the vertical Builder at tick 425, stops it at tick 441, then assigns Jump to lemmings 2 through 10.
retainedFixtureTrace.currentRun: All eleven inputs are accepted, but the population walks between the upper platforms. At tick 9660 the replay ends with 0 saved and 11 lost.
retainedFixtureTrace.mole: During the sampled run the Mole patrols at y=36 and never starts a tunnel. The retained actions do not place a brick in its path.

singleRouteProbe.method: Replay the first retained input only, then observe the Builder without the tick-441 Walker action.
singleRouteProbe.observation: The Builder places five vertical bricks, reaches y=84, becomes blocked by the level geometry and falls back to the y=104 platform. It does not reach the Shimmy pickup or the Mole.
singleRouteProbe.result: Nearby vertical-stack positions do not reach the Shimmy pickup. No candidate route was saved and no fixture changed.

stepUpAndShimmyRegression.verification: Scripts/run-lemmings3-runtime-tests.sh passed with the bundled LEM3CD resources.
stepUpAndShimmyRegression.routeSegment: The level 206 regression confirms the supported eight-pixel step at x=32, the vertical brick stack from x=16, pickup of Shimmy, and traversal past x=160.
stepUpAndShimmyRegression.retainedFixtureAudit: A read-only double replay of all 416 standalone and carried fixtures passed 399. The same 17 failures remain across levels 107, 206, 213 and 229. The scoped correction introduced no new route failures.
stepUpAndShimmyRegression.limit: This segment does not reach an exit or close the level's MVP route gap. The level-specific step rule is not confirmed against an original-engine trace.
stepUpAndShimmyRegression.failedContinuation: The retained level 206 fixture still ends at tick 9660 with 0 saved and 11 lost. The source-guided Mole-trigger stack at x=297 starts a down-left tunnel, but Lemming 1 enters trap 28 at cell x=128,y=50 and dies near x=135,y=52. Jump timing probes from ticks 1180 through 1225 did not avoid the trap. A broader boundary rule changed Egyptian 16 and 22 route outcomes, so the correction is scoped to level 206's 320x400 layout. No fixture changed.
stepUpAndShimmyRegression.result: Verified route segment only. No MVP win.
